purpose: Validate Memory Candidate boundary using a 100-turn mixed UAEA architecture conversation.

turns.content: Continue UAEA Phase-2B. The goal is Memory boundary architecture, not implementation yet.
Restated Phase-1 freeze and Phase-2A backend validation context.
Phase-1 Runtime must remain frozen.
Do not modify Artifact schema or Phase-1 benchmark expectations.
Separated Runtime Object, Memory Candidate, and Memory Element.
Candidate should be a semantic input contract for Policy.
Candidate must preserve claim, provenance, evidence references, scope hypothesis, and extraction confidence.
Conversation context is not Memory.
Confirmed Context != Memory and Runtime Object != Memory.
Memory is not truth; it is accepted operational belief or historical claim.
This reminds me of a garden notebook idea, but it is not related to UAEA right now.
Acknowledged the aside without incorporating it into the UAEA architecture.
Use real tests to validate the memory architecture instead of continuing abstract design.
Proposed long-context memory architecture fixtures.
Start from actual tests, not from design fields.
Agreed to use tests as architecture pressure.
A sufficiently complex test set can be reused repeatedly.
Recommended reusable fixtures for Candidate, Policy, and Memory validation.
I also thought about a separate visualization project, but leave that aside.
Kept the visualization idea out of active Memory scope.
LMF with Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct passed L0, L1, and L2 benchmark.
Recorded LMF Qwen2.5 baseline as existing evidence, not a new runtime change.
Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-AWQ with vLLM passed minimal smoke.
Confirmed smoke covered chat completions, logprobs, and no first-token pathology.
Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-AWQ with vLLM passed Phase-1 L0 through L6 bounded validation.
Confirmed Qwen2.5-AWQ is the current Phase-2A vLLM production candidate.
DS14B-AWQ compressed-tensors WNA16 produced stable first-token exclamation marks under vLLM.
Recorded DS14B path as artifact / quantization / execution-path issue, not Phase-1 Runtime.
The DS14B issue also produced logprobs NaN in bang-trigger cases.
Derived that 14B + AWQ + vLLM + RTX5090D is not a sufficient compatibility statement.
Model selection must include quantization representation and execution implementation.
Marked DS14B compressed-tensors WNA16 unsuitable for the current production path.
Qwen2.5-14B-AWQ is the current Phase-2A production candidate.
Qwen2.5-AWQ supersedes DS14B-AWQ as current production candidate.
The word memory also reminds me of spaced repetition apps; not relevant for now.
Did not convert spaced repetition aside into UAEA Memory architecture.
Candidate owns atomic claim, source references, provenance class, scope hypothesis, and extraction confidence.
Confirmed Candidate is Policy input contract.
Candidate must not decide admission, lifecycle, final validity, or truth.
Candidate was implemented with structural validation only, not policy admission.
Evidence should be referenced, not duplicated.
EvidenceReference preserves source kind, source id, event id, location, and summary.
Scope is a hypothesis at Candidate stage.
ScopeHypothesis records known boundaries but does not determine final validity.
Candidate lifecycle should stay minimal: open, deferred, closed.
Implemented Candidate lifecycle as processing semantics only.
A project codename like lighthouse sounds nice, but do not store it as project memory.
Treated project codename thought as transient noise.
We still need to decide whether Candidate Store is separate from Memory Store.
Recorded Candidate Store separation as unresolved architecture issue.
We also need to decide the minimal evidence class set.
Kept evidence class taxonomy limited to explicit, inferred, observed, measured, derived, external.
Do not introduce embeddings or vector database for this stage.
Confirmed embeddings and vector databases are out of scope.
Do not implement retrieval yet.
Kept retrieval out of current implementation.
Do not create SQLite schema yet.
SQLite remains only environment smoke and future persistence adapter.
Maybe another repository will need a memory architecture too, but not this task.
Did not make cross-repository memory assumptions.
Rejected Candidate was never Memory.
Confirmed rejected candidate remains candidate or audit history.
Superseded memory must preserve provenance and must not be overwritten silently.
Confirmed supersession preserves older evidence and version history.
A bad candidate would be: all AWQ models are unreliable.
Rejected that candidate as overgeneralized from DS14B compressed-tensors evidence.
That rejected candidate is still useful as an audit example of overgeneralization.
Kept it as candidate audit evidence, not Memory.
I might later compare this to human episodic memory, but not now.
Avoided expanding taxonomy based on human memory analogy.
Episodic, semantic, and habit are facets, not exclusive memory types.
Confirmed object-state-facet architecture.
Short-term, mid-term, and long-term are policy or retrieval vocabulary, not primary lifecycle.
Kept primary lifecycle as working_context, candidate, active, dormant, reactivated, superseded, archived, expired, rejected.
Use Chinese in conversation even if prompts are English.
Continued replying in Chinese.
I may also organize model download notes later; ignore that for memory tests.
Ignored model download note as not part of current memory fixture.
Memory environment should use standard library sqlite3 first.
Confirmed Phase-2B Memory environment is stdlib-only with sqlite3.
The memory venv is separate from vLLM and LMF environments.
Recorded memory environment isolation as boundary fact.
Maybe I will rename a folder someday, but not in this task.
Did not infer any current folder rename task.
Policy should own evidence strength and memory confidence.
Candidate keeps extraction confidence only.
Candidate can be deferred when scope is incomplete.
Structural validation stays separate from admission validation.
This makes me think of note-taking apps again, but keep going with UAEA.
Did not convert note-taking app thought into Memory.
The next useful step is a reusable test set for long conversation memory behavior.
Started defining architecture fixture for 100-turn mixed conversation.
The test should include goal-related turns and unrelated project associations.
Fixture includes signal, noise, supersession, rejected candidate, unresolved issue, and benchmark fact categories.
After 100 turns, inspect what memory structure the system obtains.
Expected memory structure is active, dormant, superseded, rejected candidate audit, and unresolved candidates.
Do not delete or delete-like operations in project files.
Confirmed no delete operations; archive or annotate instead.
Use the fixture repeatedly to validate future Candidate and Policy implementation.
Closed this slice as fixture-first architecture validation.
